summary: Ledgr new features (daily-summary + backup export/import) fully verified via public preview URL. 9 new tests + 30 regression tests = 39/39 passed. Daily summary correctly returns date/revenue/purchases/grossProfit/supplierPayments/drawings/netCash/counts/suppliers with correct math (revenue=100, purchases=40, grossProfit=60, supplierPayments=20, netCash=80). Backup export returns _meta{app:'ledgr', version:1, exportedAt ISO} and NO _id leakage anywhere. Import replace mode wipes then re-inserts each provided collection; omitted collections are untouched. Import merge mode upserts by id (updates existing, inserts new, leaves others). Malformed/invalid bodies return proper 4xx (Pydantic 422). No regressions in previously-working endpoints.

minor.issue: In replace mode, if a document in the list is missing the 'id' field, insert_many still accepts it and there is no server-side validation of item shape (typed as List[dict]). Consider validating each collection against its Pydantic model to catch corrupt backups before wiping.
In replace mode, DB is wiped BEFORE insert_many is executed. If insert_many fails mid-flight, the DB is left empty. Consider transaction or insert-then-swap strategy for atomicity.

Query uses {'$gte': date, '$lt': date + '\uffff'} which is a string-prefix trick. Works for stored dates like 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS', but relies on lexicographic ordering. Consider explicit end-of-day boundary ('$lt': next_day) for clarity.
Missing input validation: does not verify that 'date' matches YYYY-MM-DD format. A junk value like '?date=foo' returns 200 with zeroed data instead of 400/422.

action_items: (Optional) Add YYYY-MM-DD regex validation on /api/reports/daily-summary date query param, returning 422 for malformed dates.
(Optional) Validate each collection payload in /api/backup/import against its Pydantic model (Supplier, Bill, Sale, Payment, InventoryCheck) so corrupt/foreign backups cannot wipe real data.
(Optional) Make /api/backup/import replace mode atomic: build the new set in a temp collection or wrap in a transaction, so a mid-import failure does not leave the DB empty.
(Optional) Add pagination or a 'since' filter to /api/backup/export because the current implementation loads up to 20000 docs per collection into memory.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 707: daily-summary uses date-prefix match with '\uffff' sentinel — works but slightly fragile. Explicit next-day boundary would be more robust.
server.py line 754-761: BackupPayload accepts List[dict] instead of typed models — trades safety for flexibility. Import replace is destructive; typed models are recommended.
server.py line 780-782: `await db[name].delete_many({})` happens BEFORE `insert_many(items)`; non-atomic. If insert_many fails, DB is wiped.
server.py backup_export loads whole collections into memory (to_list(20000)). Fine for a single-user shop app; document the ceiling.
No _id leakage confirmed in backup export across all 5 collections + settings and in daily-summary.suppliers[] — verified by assertion in tests.
seed_data_creation: Each test seeds TEST_-prefixed data (suppliers, bills, sales, payments) and cleans up. A module-scoped 'full_snapshot' fixture exports the full DB before running any destructive test and restores it via /api/backup/import (mode=replace) at teardown, guaranteeing DB state is preserved across the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is stable. Regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_vocash_backend.py (30 tests) + new features suite at /app/backend/tests/test_ledgr_new_features.py (9 tests) = 39 tests, all passing against the public preview URL. If retesting, the full_snapshot fixture in test_ledgr_new_features.py MUST be used for any destructive backup tests — it exports state on entry and imports back on exit. Public URL comes from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env.
rca_of_issue: N/A — all requested features work as specified.
